1: # HTML Base Design — Style Dictionary Plan
2: 
3: **Status:** Draft
4: **Branch:** `feature/design-system-style-dictionary`
5: **Last updated:** October 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Goal
10: 
11: Make the HTML renderer's base design a **CSS-first, Style Dictionary pipeline**:
12: 
13: - Design tokens are authored in three layers (base → semantic → component).
14: - Style Dictionary generates the token CSS.
15: - The hand-authored reset and `.pathland-*` component CSS live in `design/html/` and consume
16:   the generated `var(--pl-*)` tokens.
17: - The renderer embeds the generated bundle in Rust.
18: - The design loop (edit tokens/CSS → rebuild CSS → preview) does not require changing Rust
19:   source files.
20: 
21: ## Non-goals
22: 
23: - **Multiple brands/themes.** Removed from scope.
24: - **App-selected base designs, custom app base CSS, `BaseDesign`/`BaseDesignSource` APIs, and
25:   per-app `pathland.base-design.*` configuration.** Removed from scope. The HTML renderer has
26:   one built-in base design.
27: - GTK/Qt renderer changes.
28: - Generated Java/TypeScript token constants and documentation (possible follow-up).
29: - A production hashed linked stylesheet (deferred; the renderer embeds the base CSS).
30: - Any protocol change. `spec/TOKENS.md` remains the catalog contract.
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## Architecture
35: 
36: ### Three token layers
37: 
38: | Layer | Contents | Emitted to CSS? | References |
39: |---|---|---|---|
40: | **base** | Palette (`base.color.blue.600`), spacing/type scales, radii, border widths, elevation primitives | No — resolved into literals | None |
41: | **semantic** | `color.*`, `space.base`, `font.*`, `radius.*`, `border.width.*`, `elevation.*`, `control.*`, `size.control.*`, `opacity.disabled` | Yes | base |
42: | **component** | `button.*`, `input.*`, `toggle.*`, `slider.*`, `progress.*`, `gauge.*`, `stepper.*`, `picker.*`, `menu.*`, `label.*`, `icon.*`, `spinner.*` | Yes | semantic (base only when no alias exists) |
43: 
44: - Dark values use `$extensions.pathland.dark` on each token.
45: - Base palette entries are distinct (`blue.600`, `blue.400`); semantic tokens explicitly
46:   reference the dark entry.
47: - `space.<N>` remains generative: only `space.base` is emitted. Component dimensions reference
48:   the base scale (e.g. `base.space.3`), not the generative family.
49: - `button.padding` becomes `button.padding.horizontal` / `.vertical`.
50: - Internal component tokens (durations, z-index, `em` icon sizes) are emitted but are
51:   renderer-internal, not part of `spec/TOKENS.md`.
52: 
53: ### Source and generated files
54: 
55: ```
56: design/
57:   package.json                  # style-dictionary v5, chokidar; scripts: build/dev/check
58:   package-lock.json
59:   style-dictionary.config.mjs
60:   tokens/
61:     base/*.tokens.json          # internal palette + scales
62:     semantic/*.tokens.json      # catalog semantic + shared control.*
63:     component/*.tokens.json     # full per-component token surface
64:   html/
65:     reset.css                   # preflight + html/body
66:     components.css              # .pathland-* rules, consuming var(--pl-*)
67:   scripts/
68:     build.mjs                   # SD build + concat reset+tokens+components
69:     dev.mjs                     # build + watch tokens + html/*.css
70:     check.mjs                   # layer/catalog/type/reference validation
71:   build/                        # generated, gitignored
72:     tokens.css
73:     base.css
74:     manifest.json
75:   README.md
76: lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css   # synced generated bundle (committed)
77: scripts/sync-design-css.sh
78: ```
79: 
80: ### Renderer embedding
81: 
82: ```rust
83: // lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/css.rs
84: const CSS: &str = include_str!("../assets/base.css");
85: pub fn builtin_css() -> &'static str { CSS }
86: pub const STYLE: &str = concat!("<style>", include_str!("../assets/base.css"), "</style>");
87: ```
88: 
89: - `render_document` keeps using `css::STYLE`.
90: - The synced crate copy is generated from `design/build/base.css` and committed for packaging.
91: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` fails on drift.
92: - The renderer remains stateless and a pure function of the opcode stream; the base design is
93:   compiled in.
94: 
95: ### Style Dictionary configuration
96: 
97: - Style Dictionary v5, Node ≥22, DTCG (`$value`, `$type`, `$description`, `$extensions`).
98: - Custom formats:
99:   - `pathland/css-tokens` emits:
100:     - `:root` semantic + component variables;
101:     - `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` dark layer;
102:     - `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` and `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']`;
103:     - `:root` forced-dark `--pl-dark-*` variables.
104:   - `pathland/manifest` emits `{ path, layer, type, cssVar, darkCssVar, internal }` for
105:     validation and future codegen.
106: - Reference rules:
107:   - semantic/component → emitted token: `var(--pl-<target>)` (light/dark) and
108:     `var(--pl-dark-<target>)` (forced-dark);
109:   - → base token: resolved literal;
110:   - no explicit dark value: reference the emitted target so its dark layer wins;
111:   - explicit dark extension: use it for the dark and forced-dark layers.
112: - Base tokens are filtered from the CSS output.
113: - Dimensions preserve the current `px`/`rem` values.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: ## Phases
118: 
119: ### Phase 1 — Extract the hand-authored CSS
120: 
121: **Deliverables**
122: 
123: - `design/html/reset.css` — preflight + `html`/`body` from `css.rs`, preserving the Tailwind
124:   MIT attribution.
125: - `design/html/components.css` — every `.pathland-*` rule moved verbatim.
126: - `design/html/tokens.css` — temporary hand-authored copy of the current token block
127:   (`:root`, dark media, forced-dark).
128: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` — copy the three files to
129:   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/`; `--check` mode.
130: - `css.rs` assembles the synced files with `include_str!`/`concat!`; output unchanged.
131: - Wire the sync into `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the `refresh-ide` Maven profile,
132:   and CI.
133: 
134: **Verification**
135: 
136: - `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.
137: - `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden`.
138: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check`.
139: - Rendered output is textually unchanged.
140: 
141: ### Phase 2 — Style Dictionary pipeline for the existing token surface
142: 
143: **Deliverables**
144: 
145: - `design/package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `style-dictionary.config.mjs`,
146:   `design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs`.
147: - Base/semantic/component token files covering every variable currently in
148:   `design/html/tokens.css`.
149: - Generated `design/build/tokens.css`, `design/build/base.css`,
150:   `design/build/manifest.json`.
151: - Replace the temporary `design/html/tokens.css` with the generated output.
152: - Sync `design/build/base.css` to the crate asset.
153: - `design/scripts/check.mjs` validates:
154:   - every Tier-1 catalog token is present;
155:   - semantic → base, component → semantic (base only when justified);
156:   - every emitted token has dark + forced-dark values;
157:   - no unresolved references;
158:   - internal tokens are marked.
159: 
160: **Verification**
161: 
162: - `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`.
163: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check`.
164: - `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.
165: - The generated CSS contains the four token layers and all Tier-1 variables.
166: 
167: ### Phase 3 — Full component token layer
168: 
169: **Deliverables**
170: 
171: - Add component tokens for design-relevant literal values in `components.css` and update the
172:   rules to consume them. Structural values (`display`, `flex`, `100%`, positioning) stay in
173:   CSS.
174: 
175: | Component | Tokens |
176: |---|---|
177: | Button | `button.padding.{vertical,horizontal}`, `button.line-height`, `button.border.width`, `button.focus.ring.{width,offset,color}`, `button.transition.duration`, `button.background-hover` |
178: | Icon | `icon.size`, `icon.offset` |
179: | Toggle | `toggle.gap`, `toggle.checkbox.size`, `toggle.switch.{width,height,radius}`, `toggle.thumb.{size,offset,travel}`, `toggle.transition.duration`, `toggle.focus.ring.{width,offset}` |
180: | Slider | `slider.gap`, `slider.height`, `slider.track.{height,radius}`, `slider.thumb.{size,offset,border.width}`, `slider.focus.ring.{width,offset}` |
181: | Control / Input | `control.line-height`, `control.border.width`, `control.transition.duration`, `input.padding.{vertical,horizontal}`, `input.focus.ring.{width,offset}`, `input.swatch.inset` |
182: | Progress | `progress.height`, `progress.radius` |
183: | Stepper | `stepper.gap`, `stepper.button.size`, `stepper.border.width` |
184: | Spinner | `spinner.size`, `spinner.border.width`, `spinner.duration` |
185: | Gauge | `gauge.height`, `gauge.radius`, `gauge.transition.duration` |
186: | Menu | `menu.min-width`, `menu.border.width`, `menu.z-index` |
187: | Color picker | `color.swatch.inset` |
188: 
189: - Extend `token_spec.rs` length rules so every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by
190:   `isLengthToken`.
191: - Add a validation that the SD manifest's dimension tokens all satisfy `isLengthToken`.
192: - Run `npm run regen` for the TypeScript token conventions if the lists change.
193: 
194: **Verification**
195: 
196: - `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`.
197: - `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` and `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden`.
198: - No design-relevant literal remains in `components.css`.
199: 
200: ### Phase 4 — Build, CI, docs
201: 
202: **Deliverables**
203: 
204: - `scripts/lib.sh` runs the design build + sync before `build_rust_html`.
205: - `lib/java/pom.xml` `refresh-ide` runs the design build + sync before cargo.
206: - CI: design install/build/check, sync check, cargo test, Maven tests, TS tests.
207: - `design/README.md`: three-layer model, dark extension, references, internal tokens,
208:   build/dev/check, sync, "generated files — do not edit".
209: - Update `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md` and `AGENTS.md`.
210: 
211: **Verification**
212: 
213: - Full build/test pipeline passes from a clean checkout.
214: 
215: ### Phase 5 — Design preview (development tool)
216: 
217: **Deliverables**
218: 
219: - A static preview that loads `design/build/base.css` and renders representative component
220:   markup (button, input, toggle, slider, progress, stepper, menu, media, etc.), so token/CSS
221:   changes can be reviewed with a browser refresh.
222: - Optional: a dev-only watcher that rebuilds `design/build/base.css` on token/CSS changes.
223: 
224: This is a development tool, **not** an app-selectable base design.
225: 
226: **Verification**
227: 
228: - `npm --prefix design run dev` rebuilds `design/build/base.css`.
229: - The preview reflects token and component CSS changes on refresh.
230: 
231: ---
232: 
233: ## Acceptance criteria
234: 
235: - The base design is generated from the three-layer Style Dictionary source plus hand-authored
236:   reset/component CSS.
237: - The renderer embeds the synced generated bundle; no app-facing base-design selection exists.
238: - The design token layers are validated against the protocol catalog, dark/forced-dark rules,
239:   and dimension/length conventions.
240: - `cargo test`, the Java shim tests, the TypeScript tests, and the sync check pass.
241: - No multiple-brand or app-selected base-design machinery is introduced.
242: 
243: ## Deferred
244: 
245: - Production hashed linked stylesheet for the single built-in design.
246: - SD-generated TypeScript/Java token constants and documentation.
247: - Additional preview/design-tool ergonomics beyond Phase 5.
248: 
249: ## Removed from scope
250: 
251: - Multiple brands/themes.
252: - App-selected base designs, custom app base CSS, `BaseDesign`/`BaseDesignSource`, and
253:   `pathland.base-design.*` configuration.

(End of file - total 253 lines)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the Pathland demo scripts. Source this file; it defines
# $ROOT (the repository root) and the prerequisite-build helpers each demo uses.

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Build the Rust HTML renderer cdylib (embedded in the Java pathland-render-html jar).
build_rust_html() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-render-html)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the desktop demos link: the core ring (libpathland_core)
# and the GTK4 renderer (libpathland_gtk).
build_gtk_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the Qt desktop demo links: the core ring
# (libpathland_core) and the Qt Quick renderer (libpathland_qt).
build_qt_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt)
}

# Install the Java reactor (everything except the two web demos, which need a
# newer JDK to run; they are not required to launch the other demos).
java_install() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/java" && mvn -q install -DskipTests \
    -pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo')

# Pathland Design Tokens

**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 27, 2026

---

## Purpose

Design tokens are the application-facing vocabulary for **look and feel** —
colors, typography, spacing, radii (roundings), border widths, elevations, and
control styling. They let an application **roll a full theme** — including a
**dark variant** — that is honored consistently across every renderer, while
leaving platform-native defaults and interaction-state styling to the renderer.

This document is the companion catalog for the [Design Token
System](./OPCODE.md#design-token-system). It defines:

- the **standard token catalog** (what renderers must understand),
- the **resolution contract** (override → default → parent → fallback),
- the **color-scheme contract** (base = light, `dark.` = dark), and
- the **renderer integration contract** (how future native renderers adopt it).

The wire encoding (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`, the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type)
lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md). Modifier mapping lives in
[MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md). The DSL surface is specified in
[DSL.md](./DSL.md).

> **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
> in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
> defines the protocol contract only.

---

## Core Principle

> **The application owns the theme. The renderer owns the defaults, the scheme
> detection, and the interaction states.**

- The **application** declares a theme: token overrides (base values = the
  **light** design, `dark.`-prefixed values = the **dark** design) and, in a
  style property, a **token reference** instead of a literal value.
- The **renderer** supplies platform-appropriate defaults for the standard
  catalog (both light and dark), derives the **effective color scheme** from the
  platform (OS / browser / native theme), resolves token references, and owns
  hover/pressed/focus/disabled styling.

This preserves native look-and-feel by default and gives the application
cross-renderer consistency when it overrides tokens.

### Ownership

| Aspect | Owner |
|--------|-------|
| Theme values (base + `dark.*`) | Application |
| Color-scheme detection (light/dark) | Renderer (platform-derived; app may force via `SET_COLOR_SCHEME`) |
| Default token values (light + dark) | Renderer |
| Token resolution (override → default → parent → fallback) | Renderer |
| Interaction states (hover/pressed/focus/disabled) | Renderer |
| Literal property values | Application |

---

## Token Identification

Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** — `color.primary`,
`font.body.size`, `space.2` — case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. A `dark.`
prefix selects the **dark variant** of a token (`dark.color.primary`).

The path namespace is **open**: the standard catalog below is a contract the
renderer MUST implement; any path outside it is **application-defined** and
renderer-optional (the renderer falls back rather than erroring).

---

## Value Types

A token's value uses the standard [value types](./OPCODE.md#value-types) —
`COLOR` (packed `0xAARRGGBB`, sRGB), `F32`, `U32`, `I32`, `U8`, `STRING`, `ENUM`.

A **token reference** in a property uses the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`):
`C` = arenaRef to the token path. A property carries **exactly one** value —
either a literal (`COLOR`/`F32`/…) or a token reference, never both (see
[References in properties](#references-in-properties)).

---

## Standard Token Catalog

The catalog is layered. **Tier 1 (core)** tokens are mandatory: a renderer MUST
provide light and dark defaults and resolve them. **Tier 2 (extended)** tokens
are recommended: a renderer SHOULD provide defaults, and an application MAY
override them; a renderer that cannot apply a Tier 2 token ignores it (the same
"allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).

Default values are **renderer-owned and platform-appropriate**; the tables below
name the tokens and their *meaning*, never concrete values. The renderer MUST
resolve tokens by name and MAY map them onto native semantic resources (e.g. the
platform's system text color for `color.text.primary`).

### Colors — Tier 1

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
| `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
| `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
| `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
| `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
| `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
| `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
| `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
| `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |

Tier 2: `color.separator` (hairline dividers), and status colors
`color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`.

### Typography — Tier 1 core

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `font.body.size` | Body text size |
| `font.body.weight` | Body text weight (100–900) |
| `font.body.family` | Body font family (STRING) |

Tier 2: `font.body.lineHeight`, `font.caption.size`,
`font.heading.1.size`–`font.heading.6.size` (with matching `.weight`/`.family`
paths), `font.mono.family`.

The **predefined typographies** (`TEXT_STYLE`: `LargeTitle`…`Caption2`,
spec/MODIFIERS.md §2) are the semantic counterparts of these token paths: the
renderer owns their concrete size/weight (a baked per-renderer HIG scale). An
application that wants full control can instead bind text to a `TEXT_STYLE` of
its own via the `font.<style>.*` token paths above, or set an explicit
`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_FAMILY` override on top.

### Spacing — Tier 1

Spacing is a **generative family** (Tailwind-v4 style): one base unit
multiplied by an arbitrary number.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `space.base` | The spacing **unit** (F32) — override this to change the whole density |
| `space.<N>` | `space.base` × N, where N is any positive decimal (`space.1`, `space.2`, `space.0.5`, `space.3.75`) — **computed** by the resolver |

Rules:

1. The `space.<N>` family is **generative**, not independently valued: the
   renderer resolves `space.base` and multiplies by the numeric leaf. Individual
   members MUST NOT be overridden via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` — override `space.base`
   to control the whole scale.
2. The color-scheme layer and parent fallback apply to `space.base`, never to an
   individual `space.<N>` member (`dark.space.2` is not a token; the dark layer
   is `dark.space.base`).
3. A spacing/padding property MAY carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to any
   `space.<N>` path — e.g. a DSL expresses `.padding(space.2)` or `Space(2)`.
   Literal F32 spacing values remain valid and unthemed.

Tier 2: `size.control.xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` — standard control heights.

### Radius (roundings) — Tier 1

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `radius.xs` / `radius.sm` / `radius.md` / `radius.lg` / `radius.xl` | Corner radius scale (F32) |
| `radius.full` | Fully round (pill/circle) — renderer resolves to its "infinite" value |

### Borders — Tier 1 core

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `border.width.thin` | Default hairline/border width |

Tier 2: `border.width.thick`.

### Elevation — Tier 2

Shadows are composite; each component is its own token:

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `elevation.low.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | Low elevation shadow |
| `elevation.high.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | High elevation shadow |

### Opacity — Tier 2

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `opacity.disabled` | The renderer MAY apply this to disabled controls. The disabled **state** itself is the `ENABLED` property; its visual handling (including this opacity) remains renderer-owned. |

### Shared control core — Tier 1

Tokens every control-style component (buttons, inputs, switches, sliders, …)
shares. Renderers MUST resolve these; an individual token a renderer cannot
apply is ignored.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `control.background` | Control resting background |
| `control.foreground` | Control content (label/icon) color |
| `control.border` | Control border color |
| `control.border.width` | Control border width |
| `control.radius` | Control corner radius |
| `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |
| `control.height` | Control height (F32) |
| `control.font.size` / `control.font.weight` | Control text |
| `control.accent` | Control accent (fill, selection, focus) |

### Per-component tokens

Small sets; only where a component's semantics genuinely differ from
`control.*`. All Tier 1 unless noted.

**Buttons** (Tier 1): `button.background`, `button.foreground`, `button.border`,
`button.radius`, `button.padding`, `button.height`, `button.font.size`,
`button.font.weight`, `button.accent`.

> A composite shorthand such as `button.padding` (two-axis) is renderer-owned:
> the scalar token value types cannot encode a multi-part CSS shorthand. Apps
> that need a scalar override should use the shared control padding tokens or
> per-component properties.

**Text fields / editors** (Tier 1): `input.background`, `input.foreground`,
`input.placeholder`, `input.border`, `input.radius`, `input.font.size`.

**Toggle / switch** (Tier 1): `toggle.accent`, `toggle.track.off`,
`toggle.track.on`, `toggle.thumb`.

**Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.

**Progress / gauge** (Tier 1): `progress.track`, `progress.fill`,
`gauge.track`, `gauge.fill`.

**Stepper** (Tier 2): `stepper.accent`, `stepper.background`, `stepper.border`,
`stepper.radius`.

**Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,
`picker.radius`.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
      # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
      # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
      # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
      # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
      # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
      # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
      # are installed in the next step.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
            gstreamer1.0-libav

      - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            qt6-base-dev \
            qt6-declarative-dev \
            qt6-declarative-private-dev \
            qt6-multimedia-dev \
            qml6-module-qtqml \
            qml6-module-qtqml-models \
            qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
            qml6-module-qtquick \
            qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
            qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
            qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
            qml6-module-qtquick-window \
            qml6-module-qtmultimedia
        # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
        # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
        # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
        # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
        # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
        # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
          npm run build

      # The demos serve the committed bundle from their static resource dirs
      # (content-hashed dom-renderer-<sha256>.js + the dom-renderer.current
      # pointer; stale hashed copies are pruned); copying the freshly built one
      # must not change the working tree.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm run copy-to-demos
          git diff --exit-code -- lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources

      # Real-browser guard for the per-window-id service worker: the browser-variance
      # bugs (WebKit reports an empty clientId on navigations; relative cache keys are
      # rejected) only appear in a real worker engine, never in jsdom/happy-dom.
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit

      - name: Service worker E2E (Chromium + WebKit)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npm run test:e2e

---

## Color Schemes (Light / Dark)

Base token paths define the **light** design. A `dark.`-prefixed path defines
the **dark** design for the same token.

The renderer derives the **effective color scheme** from its platform's native
light/dark signal by default. An application MAY override it for the whole host
with `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` (`platform` / `light` / `dark`); the renderer
applies the override until the application restores `platform`. The
platform-derived signal itself is never carried by the protocol.

### Rules

1. **Base = light.** `color.primary` is the light value; `dark.color.primary`
   is the dark value.
2. A renderer MUST provide **both** light and dark defaults for every Tier 1
   token (platform-appropriate). Dark mode therefore works even when the
   application only overrides base tokens.
3. The application rolls a full theme by overriding base values and — where the
   dark look must differ — `dark.*` values.
4. The renderer MUST **re-resolve** every token-referencing property when the
   effective scheme changes (including a `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` override), and MAY
   animate the transition.
5. A **`DESIGN_TOKEN` reference** whose path starts with `dark.` is an
   **explicit dark-variant reference**: it resolves the bare path against the
   dark layer regardless of the active scheme. (A `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override
   still uses the `dark.` prefix to select the dark layer.)
6. The `dark.` prefix is the first scheme prefix; the namespace is open so
   custom schemes could follow. Only `light` (base) and `dark` are
   standardized.

---

## Resolution

```
FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath, scheme):
    # Walk most-specific → least-specific, applying the dark layer first.
    layers = []
    if scheme == dark:
        layers += [dark.path, dark.parent(path), …dark.root]   # dark.* layer
    layers += [path, parent(path), …root]                       # base layer

    for candidate in layers:
        if appOverrides.has(candidate):
            return appOverrides[candidate]
    for candidate in layers:
        if rendererDefaults.has(candidate):
            return rendererDefaults[candidate]
    return fallbackValue(path)
```

Example — `color.primary` with the **dark** scheme active and only
`dark.color.primary` overridden:

1. `dark.color.primary` — app override → **used**.
2. (Unreached) `color.primary` app override, `dark.color.primary` renderer
   default, etc.

With the **light** scheme active:

1. `color.primary` — app override, else renderer default, else parent/fallback.
   The `dark.*` layer is skipped entirely.

### Generative token families

A **generative family** is a token rule rather than an independent value. Today
the `space` family is generative: `space.<N>` resolves by resolving `space.base`
(the scheme layer and parent fallback apply there) and multiplying by the
numeric leaf parsed from the path. This lets one override (`space.base`) drive
an arbitrarily fine spacing scale without per-step tokens. Only the `space`
family is generative today; other families could follow.

---

## References in properties

Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY instead
carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`** value type (`0x08`), with `C` = arenaRef to the
token path. The renderer resolves the reference against the token tables and the
current scheme, and re-resolves when the scheme changes.

- This is how a DSL expresses *semantic intent*: `.foregroundStyle(.primary)`
  or `Color.token("color.primary")` emits a token reference, not a packed color.
- A literal value and a token reference are mutually exclusive on a property.
- Because overrides and the scheme are renderer state, a token-typed property
  requires **no re-emission** when a token changes — the renderer re-resolves.
- If a reference cannot be resolved (no override, no renderer default), the
  property is **left unset** and the renderer's own default styling applies;
  resolution NEVER errors and MUST NOT retain a previously resolved value.
- `META::RESET_THEME` clears every application override (base + `dark.*`) and
  re-resolves all token-referencing properties against the renderer defaults.
  A replacement theme is emitted as `RESET_THEME` followed by its
  `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in the same frame.

---

## Renderer Responsibilities

A renderer MUST:

1. Provide platform-appropriate **light and dark defaults** for all Tier 1
   tokens.
2. Accept `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides, and clear
   them on `META::RESET_THEME`.
3. Derive the effective color scheme from the platform (or honor
   `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`) and re-resolve on change.
4. Resolve token references (`DESIGN_TOKEN` value type) in properties, including
   explicit `dark.` references.
5. Fall back to defaults when no override exists; leave the property unset when
   the reference cannot be resolved.
6. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.

A renderer MAY:

- Map tokens onto native semantic resources (system colors, platform
  typography) for its defaults.
- **Ignore** individual tokens it cannot apply (Tier 2, or Tier 1 tokens
  without a native equivalent) — the "allowed and ignored" rule modifiers use.
- Quantize / approximate token values to platform capabilities (e.g. RGB565
  color depth on embedded displays, limited font sets).

An application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base and `dark.*`)
and reference any token in a property; it MUST NOT assume specific default
values.

---

## Renderer Integration Contract

A future native renderer adopts the token system by implementing five pieces:

1. **Default token table** — Tier 1 light + dark defaults from native resources.
2. **Scheme detection** — the platform's native light/dark signal.
3. **Resolution** — the override → default → parent → fallback algorithm, with
   the `dark.*` layer keyed on the effective scheme.
4. **Property resolution** — any property carrying a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference
   resolves to the concrete native value (e.g. a dynamic system color / theme
   resource / style value).
5. **Re-resolution** — on scheme change, re-resolve and update the rendered
   output; animate if native.

The same contract powers the reference renderers (`pathland-render-html`,
`pathland-render-gtk`, the JS DOM renderer) and is checked in their `status.md`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sync the generated HTML base design into the Rust renderer crate.
#
# The canonical source lives in design/ (Style Dictionary tokens + hand-authored
# reset/components CSS). `design/build/base.css` is the generated bundle the
# renderer embeds with `include_str!`. Run `npm --prefix design run build` first.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/sync-design-css.sh           copy the bundle into the crate
#   scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check   fail if the committed crate copy drifted
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/design/build/base.css"
DEST_DIR="$ROOT/lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets"
DEST="$DEST_DIR/base.css"

check=0
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
  check=1
elif [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "usage: $0 [--check]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! -f "$SRC" ]]; then
  echo "sync-design-css: missing $SRC — run 'npm --prefix design run build' first" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ $check -eq 1 ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$DEST" ]]; then
    echo "sync-design-css: missing $DEST — run scripts/sync-design-css.sh" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! diff -u "$DEST" "$SRC"; then
    echo "sync-design-css: crate CSS is stale — run 'npm --prefix design run build && scripts/sync-design-css.sh'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "sync-design-css: up to date"
  exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
cp "$SRC" "$DEST"
echo "sync-design-css: wrote $DEST"

input.content:
# Pathland base design

The built-in look of the HTML renderer, generated from a **three-layer Style
Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS.

```
tokens/base/*.tokens.json        internal palette + scales          (not emitted)
tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json    protocol catalog semantics        (emitted)
tokens/component/*.tokens.json   per-component surface             (emitted)
html/reset.css                   Tailwind-derived preflight        (hand-authored)
html/components.css              .pathland-* rules                 (hand-authored)
```

The generated bundle is `build/base.css` (reset + `tokens.css` + components).
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` is the synced, committed
copy the renderer embeds with `include_str!`; the renderer has one built-in base
design and no app-facing design selection.

## Commands

```sh
npm --prefix design ci          # install (CI / clean checkout)
npm --prefix design run build   # Style Dictionary + build/base.css
npm --prefix design run check   # catalog/layer/dark/dimension validation
npm --prefix design run dev     # rebuild on token/CSS changes
npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve   # also serve preview/ on :4173
scripts/sync-design-css.sh      # copy build/base.css into the Rust crate
scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
```

After changing tokens or CSS: `npm --prefix design run build`, then
`scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, then run `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.

`build/` and `node_modules/` are gitignored. `package-lock.json` is committed.

## Tokens

Each token is a flat DTCG entry: `$value`, `$type`, optional `$description` and
`$extensions.pathland`. Keys carry their full dotted path because the catalog
contains paths that are both a leaf and a group (`control.border` is a color,
`control.border.width` is a dimension), which nested DTCG trees cannot represent.

- **base** tokens are literals. They are internal: the generator resolves them
  to literals and **never emits them** as CSS variables. Override the semantic
  or component token instead.
- **semantic** tokens reference base tokens. They are the protocol catalog
  surface (`spec/TOKENS.md`).
- **component** tokens reference semantic tokens, or a base scale token
  (`base.space.*`, `base.radius.*`, `base.border.width.*`, `base.size.*`,
  `base.font.*`) when no semantic alias exists. A component token that must
  reference a base **color** needs an explicit justification:

  ```json
  "$extensions": {
    "pathland": { "baseReference": "why this base color is used directly" }
  }
  ```

### Dark values

Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`:

```json
{
  "color.primary": {
    "$value": "{base.color.blue.600}",
    "$type": "color",
    "$extensions": { "pathland": { "dark": "{base.color.blue.400}" } }
  }
}
```

The generator emits four token layers:

1. `:root` (light),
2. `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-pathland-scheme])`,
3. `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` (forced dark) and
   `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']` (forced light),
4. the forced-dark variable family `--pl-dark-*` for explicit `dark.` token
   references.

A reference to another **emitted** token compiles to `var(--pl-<target>)` (and
`var(--pl-dark-<target>)` in the forced-dark family), so the target's dark layer
wins. A reference to a **base** token compiles to its literal. With no explicit
dark value, the dark layers reference the same target variable.

### Internal tokens

Durations, z-index, and `em` icon sizes are renderer-internal (not part of
`spec/TOKENS.md`). Mark them with `$extensions.pathland.internal: true`; they are
still emitted and listed in `build/manifest.json` with `"internal": true`.

## Validation

`npm run check` enforces:

- every Tier-1 token in `pathland_core::TIER1_TOKENS` is present;
- layer direction (semantic → base, component → semantic/base scale) and
  no unresolved references;
- every emitted token has light, platform-dark, forced-dark-scheme, and
  forced-dark variable declarations;
- every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by the canonical
  `isLengthToken` rules in `pathland-render-html::token_spec` (add a rule there
  when introducing a new dimension path);
- durations / z-index / icon sizes are marked internal;
- `build/manifest.json` and `build/tokens.css` match the current sources, and
  base tokens are not emitted.

## Preview

`preview/index.html` loads `build/base.css` and renders representative
`.pathland-*` markup (buttons, fields, toggles, slider, progress, stepper, menu,
media) with a light/dark/system switcher. Run `npm run dev -- --serve` and open
<http://127.0.0.1:4173/>. This is a development tool, not an app-selectable base
design.

## Generated files — do not edit

- `build/tokens.css`
- `build/manifest.json`
- `build/base.css`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` (synced copy)

Edit the token files or `html/{reset,components}.css`, then rebuild and sync.

Implemented the full plan in `design/PLAN.md`.

**What landed**
- Three-layer Style Dictionary pipeline: `design/tokens/{base,semantic,component}` (flat DTCG, dark extensions, internal tokens).
- Hand-authored `design/html/{reset,components}.css`; component rules now consume tokens only.

- Extended `token_spec.rs` length rules and regenerated the TS token conventions + demo DOM bundles.
- Wired design build/sync into `scripts/lib.sh`, Maven `refresh-ide`, and a new CI design job.
- Updated `status.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `design/README.md`.

- `mvn -q -B -pl pathland-render-html -am test` and `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`
- `npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve` preview smoke test

    <name>Pathland Render HTML</name>
    <description>
        The Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer (dev.pathland.render.html): a
        thin JNA shim over libpathland_render_html (pathland_html_render /
        _render_fragment / _free). Stateless: each call renders
        a full snapshot frame to HTML in one pass. The server-side/remote-projection
        target, usable from Spring Boot, Quarkus, or any Java server. The single
        renderer is the Rust crate reused by every language.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust renderer cdylib; absent the
                         dylib, the shim tests are skipped via an assumption. -->
                    <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Embed the Rust renderer dylib in the jar so it travels with the
                 artifact (JNA extracts it at runtime — no java.library.path needed).
                 Copies the host-platform build into META-INF/native/. Fails loudly
                 when the dylib is missing (the CI rust job builds it; locally run
                 cargo build first). -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>embed-native-renderer</id>
                        <phase>process-resources</phase>
                        <configuration>
                            <target>
                                <!-- Determine the platform library extension. -->
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dylib">
                                    <os family="mac" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dll">
                                    <os family="windows" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".so">
                                    <os family="unix" />
                                </condition>
                                <property name="pathland.native.ext" value="" />

                                     this copies each into META-INF/native/<os>-<arch>/.
                                     A local build has no staging dir and instead
                                     embeds the host Rust debug build in the flat
                                     META-INF/native/ layout. -->
                                <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the Java + GTK4 desktop demo: the shared demo views (SplitNavDemo) under
# the native GTK renderer, over the libpathland_core shared ring.
#
# macOS must run GTK on the main thread (-XstartOnFirstThread); Linux needs no flag.
set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib.sh"

build_gtk_dylibs
java_install

case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin)  EXT=".dylib"; MAINTHREAD="-XstartOnFirstThread" ;;
  Linux)   EXT=".so";    MAINTHREAD="" ;;
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) EXT=".dll"; MAINTHREAD="" ;;
  *) echo "unsupported OS: $(uname -s)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

cd "$ROOT/lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo"

CPFILE="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$CPFILE"' EXIT
mvn -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile="$CPFILE"
CP="target/classes:$(cat "$CPFILE")"

exec java $MAINTHREAD \
  -Dpathland.core.lib="$ROOT/lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_core$EXT" \
  -Dpathland.gtk.lib="$ROOT/lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_gtk$EXT" \
  -cp "$CP" com.pathland.demo.gtk.GtkHost

When you edit a token under `design/tokens/**`, the change has to flow into the embedded Rust CSS before the SSR demos see it.

**Fast visual loop (no demo server)**

```sh
npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/ — it rebuilds `design/build/base.css` on every token/CSS change.

**Run the actual HTML/SSR demos**

The demo scripts already do the whole chain now (`build_design` → sync → `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` → `mvn install`), so just rerun:

```sh
scripts/run-quarkus-demo.sh   # Quarkus SSR + WS demo
scripts/run-spring-demo.sh    # Spring Boot demo
```

If a demo is already running, stop it first — the Rust dylib is embedded in the installed `pathland-render-html` jar at startup.

**Before committing**

```sh
npm --prefix design run check
scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
cargo test -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-html-golden
```

Note: the GTK/Qt desktop demos do **not** consume `design/` tokens — they use their native renderer defaults, so token edits won't show there.
